parsed.explanation: A protective, traveller-facing regime with no documented exposure specific to trans visitors. Gender expression is not criminalised; self-declaration recognition exists (climate signal, not a visitor protection); a 2024 hate-crime statute explicitly covers gender identity, backed by an incitement statute with gender identity added; public support is high and queer infrastructure visible nationwide. No documented border friction, police targeting of trans travellers, or trans-specific killings. Deductions are for documented negatives: rising recorded hate crime and a 2025 study finding increased anti-LGBT prejudice; a pending amendment that would limit a gender certificate 'for imprisonment' plus one custodial case; a single centralised gender-care pathway with multi-year waits; no nonbinary marker for X-marker passports; and a total absence of documented visitor-specific remedy or border practice. Strong law but thin documented enforcement-for-visitors places it just below the 0.85 tier.

entry_documents.exposure: Foreign passports carrying an X marker have no domestic nonbinary equivalent; no documented border rule on marker mismatch.
entry_documents.protection: No criminalisation of gender expression; self-declaration framework signals trans-respecting document culture.
entry_documents.interaction: Border practice undocumented, so no evidence of adverse screening, but also no documented safeguard.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Amendment limiting a gender certificate 'for the purposes of imprisonment' passed first stage; one trans woman with a certificate convicted in 2022, acquitted 2024.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: No statute penalising presentation; the 2024 acquittal and judicial criticism of government inaction.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: A detained visitor would face placement rules shaped by the pending amendment; remedy untested.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Custodial placement by birth sex is the direction of the pending amendment; hospital ward rules unstated.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Facility exposure arises only via detention or hospitalisation; no general-access ban documented.

care_services.exposure: Single public trans health provider, 2.5–10 year first-appointment waits, documented denials on welfare/ADHD grounds.
care_services.protection: Gender-affirming care legal; NHS defends multidisciplinary model; private and self-administered routes exist.
care_services.interaction: Resident-facing bottleneck; a visitor needing continuity of HRT has no documented pathway or refusal record.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: 2025 university study finds increased anti-LGBT prejudice; recorded hate crime up 15% (mostly racism/xenophobia); a council cancelled a drag storytime.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Criminal Justice (Hate Offences) Act 2024 covers gender identity; 1989 Act incitement grounds extended 2022; official apologies; 61% public support.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Law and institutions sit on the protective side; hostility is societal and diffuse, not state-framed.

minors_guardians.exposure: No nonbinary recognition; gender care restricted for minors; conversion therapy not banned; 16–17 extension only recommended, not enacted.
minors_guardians.protection: Ministerial recommendation to extend self-declaration to 16–17 with parental consent.
minors_guardians.interaction: A guardian travelling with a trans minor finds no visitor-specific obstacle, but resident-facing care limits signal thin support.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Rising recorded hate crime and reported prejudice increase; no population denominator; no trans-specific killing documented.
street_violence_police_response.protection: Hate-crime statute with gender identity; anonymous reporting form; visible, dispersed queer scene; enforcement not shown failing.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Violence axis undocumented for trans people specifically; general reporting data cannot be attributed to gender identity.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: No documented visitor-facing remedy, ombudsman or border complaint mechanism; a hate-speech backdown report is paywalled and unverified.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Hate-crime reporting form, rights information, equal-status links, consular access assumed.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Recourse exists in principle but is unproven in operation for a short-stay foreigner.

anchor_checks.comparison: Similar: statutory gender-identity protection, no criminalisation, functional institutions. Lower here because 0.85-A documents police training, an independent oversight board and concrete apologies/compensation, while this dossier documents only a reporting form, a rising-prejudice study and a pending imprisonment-limiting amendment.

Higher here: 0.75-C documents secondary screening, brief detention, wide officer discretion and uncertain border practice; this dossier records no border friction, no detention of visitors, and a stronger hate-crime statute, though both share wide undocumented frontline discretion.

Clearly higher: 0.55-B documents visitors routed to secondary interview, refused admission and luggage searches on document divergence. Here there is no documented adverse border outcome at all, and protections are statutory rather than discretionary.

parsed.synthesis: The operative regime is protective in law and largely accepting in society, with no documented trans-specific criminal statute, border practice, police targeting or lethal violence. What lowers the score is not a traveller-facing restriction but a documented cluster: rising recorded hate crime and a 2025 study of increasing anti-LGBT prejudice, a single centralised gender-care pathway with multi-year waits, no nonbinary marker matching a foreign X passport, an amendment heading toward birth-sex custodial placement, and the absence of any documented remedy or border practice a visitor could rely on. Under burden-of-proof symmetry, the documented positives (2024 hate-crime act, incitement grounds, high public support, visible scene) outweigh undocumented friction, but silence on visitor-facing enforcement keeps it below the 0.85 tier.
